name: Naledi — funding the delivery kit
basis: Synthetic Treasury example. The R120,000 kit and operating assumptions are identical in every alternative. No entries are saved or posted.
assumptions: Opening funding-account cash R50,000 is a test assumption, not a balance established from Naledi’s incomplete history.
All alternatives acquire the same R120,000 kit on 1 November 2026. This is a Treasury funding comparison, not a different equipment choice.
Common operating cash surplus is R5,000 at each monthly payment date for 36 months. It is synthetic settled cash, not inferred receipts from historical revenue.
Senior debt: 12% fixed annual rate, 36 equal-principal monthly repayments. Mixed: R90,000 senior plus R30,000 junior at 18%, monthly interest and principal repaid at month 12.
ACT/365F, half-up rounding to cents, no fees, defaults, business-day adjustments, floating rates, VAT, tax or depreciation. These omissions must be resolved for advice.
Balances are end-of-day: same-date loan drawdown and kit payment net together; this does not establish intraday payment ordering.
All debt is repaid at the shared horizon. The cash-only alternative exposes an immediate R70,000 funding shortfall.
